brief: The Market Ear argues Q3 earnings season arrives with the bar exceptionally high, not with a collapse imminent. S&P 500 EPS sits 14% above its 90+ year trend channel (DB), and real S&P 500 earnings run well above their 30-year trend (FactSet), with actual EPS growth outpacing what real GDP would imply (BofA Quant). AI infrastructure stocks drive roughly half of S&P 500 EPS growth (FactSet). Hyperscaler capex keeps growing but decelerates in 2027, and rising hyperscaler depreciation should increasingly offset AI-capex-beneficiary earnings. Goldman estimates fully expensing capex would cut consensus 2027 S&P 500 EPS by 22%, one of the widest reported-versus-fully-expensed gaps in recent decades. Semiconductor gross margins sit at multi-decade highs, with memory margins near 80%, more than double their historical average, and consensus expects that to continue. But semiconductor earnings revisions have started rolling over (Pictet), and S&P 500 earnings growth is highly sensitive to that margin trajectory. Median S&P 500 company profit margins are also near record highs. The note does not call an earnings collapse. It says perfection has become the baseline, so no disaster is needed to create trouble.
